description: The run: starting the project, stopping it, or booting it once to see whether it comes up clean. start keeps it running and collecting output until it quits or is stopped, windowed where there is a display and headless where there is not, unless headless says otherwise; only runtime_capture needs the window. A run that quits on its own is kept, so a scene that prints an answer and quits is start, then editor_output until running is false. What runs is a scene: a SceneTree script is not an entry point here, so put the script on the root of a scene of its own and name that in scene. args hands the game its own flags, the ones it reads with OS.get_cmdline_user_args(), and a run carrying any is started by this server rather than by the editor. check boots it headless for a few frames, waits for it to quit, and answers with the verdict: whether it came up, and every error and warning it printed on the way. start and check both wait first for a scan the open editor is running and for the class cache it writes just after, since a game booted in between resolves no global class, as does every other engine this server starts on the project; waitedForEditorScanMs says how long, and scanNote says when a scan ran past thirty seconds and the game started during it. Then whatever changed on disk since it was imported is imported, and named under importedFirst. A start waits for the game to become something the runtime_* tools can talk to and says which it is under runtime: listening with the port it took, or why not, so the first call after a start does not have to be made twice. When it is not listening, mayYetAnnounce says whether that is final: false is a runtime that is not coming, true is a game still on its way up, which editor_status will see and runtimeWaitMs waits longer for, and the note then says what a runtime_* call naming no projectPath meets until it announces. A start this server made also answers with transcript, the file both the run's streams are written to, so a watch on it can be armed off the start rather than off a second call. A game that restarts itself with OS.set_restart_on_exit stays one run: editor_output and editor_status follow the process it restarted into and name those before it under restartedFrom, and stop ends it. Operations: start (needs projectPath): run the project until it quits or is stopped; stop: end the run, asking the game to close first unless graceful is false, naming the process ended under endedPid, and answer with the errors and warnings it printed under entries (editor_output has the rest); a game that started processes of its own keeps them unless andChildren says to end those too; check (needs projectPath): boot headless, quit after a few frames, and report the verdict: booted is true only for a run that quit on its own within timeoutMs, exited 0 and printed no error, so a game that reached _ready and then raised an error answers false; wait: wait for the run to end, then answer as editor_output does; profile: where the run spends its time by GDScript function, while it runs or after it ended, sorted by self time. A run started with profile: true is profiled from its start; a game the editor plays that was not is profiled from the moment this is asked; a run this server started without it is refused, since its debugger is fixed as it starts. Default start. The tool reference in the gdharness skill, and the site, say what every field of the answer means.

andChildren.description: stop: also end what the game started for itself, with OS.create_process or otherwise, such as a bench's workers and whatever those started in turn. Only the processes under the run's, to any depth, that are games of this project are ended: announced as one, or this project's engine run with --path on this project by its command line, which is how a bench whose workers deliberately carry no runtime is reached. They are named under endedChildren, with what identified each under identifiedBy; any other process under the run is left and named under childrenLeft, and childrenUnknown is true when nothing could be listed, with the note saying whether the platform would not or the run has no process to list under. Default false, and the run's process is ended either way. Only for op stop.

args.description: The game's own arguments, what OS.get_cmdline_user_args() answers, such as ["--level=2"]. The separator is added here, so a flag the engine reads goes to the game instead, and the answer says so under argsNote. A run with any is started by this server rather than by the editor, which fixes the game's command line when it opens the project, so its debugger is the keeper holding it rather than the editor; the debug_* tools answer for it all the same. Only for ops start, check.

callersOf.description: profile: also answer, under callers, where the project's scripts name this function in code: its name, or Class.name for the functions of one class. Each place has its script, line, the named function it is written in (within), whether the function is called there or passed on as a Callable (called), and the profile's calls, self and total milliseconds for the function it is in, those taking the most time first, forty at most. Found by name in the source, since the engine's profiler records nothing about who made a call, so a method of the same name on another class is listed too, except, when Class.name was asked, one called through another class of the project by name or through a parameter, local or class variable declared as one, and a call made through a string is not. A parameter, local or class variable of the same name is not the function and is not listed. A property's get or set block, which the profile names Class.@name_getter or Class.@name_setter, is asked about by that name or by the property's: the places are where the property is named, each saying instead of called whether it writes the property (access write), which runs the set block, or reads it (access read), which runs the get block, and the rows are both blocks'. Inside the property's own blocks its name is the value stored, which the engine reads and writes without running them, so those lines are not places. Only for op profile.

engineArgs.description: The engine's own flags, before the separator, such as ["--verbose"] or ["--max-fps", "60"], a value going as the next entry. Only those that change what the engine logs, draws for debugging, checks on the GPU, which renderer draws, how it times frames or whether it builds the tree a screen reader reads, and Movie Maker's --write-movie: --verbose, --quiet, --debug-collisions, --debug-paths, --debug-navigation, --debug-avoidance, --debug-stringnames, --debug-canvas-item-redraw, --debug-mute-audio, --print-fps, --gpu-profile, --gpu-validation, --gpu-abort, --disable-vsync, --frame-delay, --time-scale, --fixed-fps, --max-fps, --resolution, --write-movie, --rendering-driver, --rendering-method, --accessibility. Any other is refused, since the engine's command line can also run scripts, open other projects and write files. --rendering-driver takes vulkan, d3d12, metal, opengl3, opengl3_es, opengl3_angle or dummy, and --rendering-method forward_plus, mobile or gl_compatibility, so the same scene can be measured on another driver and a project's OpenGL fallback exercised on a machine that has Vulkan; they choose what draws a run with a window. --accessibility always has the game build the tree a screen reader reads, as the project's accessibility/general/accessibility_support at Always Active does, so runtime_inspect accessibility can read it; otherwise the engine builds it only when a screen reader is running. --write-movie takes an absolute path outside the project, in a directory that exists, ending in .avi (one file, video and sound) or .png (one numbered PNG per frame and a .wav beside them), where nothing it would write is there already; it needs a start with headless: false, since the engine crashes writing a movie headless, and it records at the project's editor/movie_writer/fps unless --fixed-fps says otherwise. --fixed-fps gives every frame the same game time and stops holding frames to the clock, which --max-fps does not undo, so with no window's refresh to wait on a headless game races ahead: given --fixed-fps 60 one ran about 450,000 frames, two hours of game time, in a second, and an animation or timer was over before the next call reached it. A headless start given it says so under framesNote. A headless game keeps to the clock without it, and --max-fps alone caps its frames. A run with any is started by this server, as one with args is. A check given --verbose answers with everything printed rather than only errors and warnings, since what verbose adds, the instances leaked at exit among it, is printed as ordinary lines. Only for ops start, check.

env.description: Environment variables for this run alone, as a map of strings, over the server's own environment. Like savesIn, a run carrying any is started by this server rather than played by the editor. Names beginning with GDHARNESS_ are refused: they are this server's contract with the addon in the game, and the runtime directory is set here whatever the rest of the environment says, so a game that moves TEMP still announces where this server looks. Only for ops start, check.

executable.description: start: an exported build to run instead of the project, as a path inside the project such as export/windows/game.exe, so what a player runs can be measured. It takes args, engineArgs, savesIn, env, headless and visible as the project does, goes on the hidden desktop the same way, and is ended by stop, but takes no scene (its pack holds the main scene) and no profile, and has no debugger: a release build quits when given one. Its runtime is not waited for. Only for op start.

frames.description: check: frames to run before quitting. Default 3. Only for op check.

graceful.description: stop, and a start that ends the run going before it: ask the game to close first, the way a player's close asks it, so its own handling of a close runs, which a game keeping a crash mark needs to take the mark down. The runtime addon delivers the close request to every node and then the root window's close_requested, and a tree with auto_accept_quit on then quits. The game is given ten seconds to exit, GDHARNESS_CLOSE_WAIT_MS sets another, and is ended the ordinary way when it does not, or when it has no runtime listening, refuses the close, or does not answer within three seconds, as a game held at a breakpoint does not; notClosedBecause (previousRunNotClosedBecause on a start) then says which. Default true; false ends the process at once. Only for ops start, stop.

headless.description: start: force a window or no window. The editor plays a game headless only when the project's editor/run/main_run_args holds --headless, so a headless start of a project whose editor plays with a window is started by this server instead, and the answer says so. Only for op start.

limit.description: profile: how many functions to answer with, those with the most self time. Default 30. Only for op profile.

mark.description: profile: answer as usual and set the run's mark at these totals, so a later profile with since: "mark" answers for one action, a press or a commit, apart from the boot and everything before it. The mark is kept beside the run's profile, so a server that replaces this one reads it too, and setting it again moves it. Given with since, the answer counts from the mark before it moves, which times one span after another. Default false. Only for op profile.

pid.description: stop: a game of this project that no server here is holding, by its process id as editor_status lists it under runtimes: one a server before a reconnect started and left no note for, or one started some other way. It is ended only when it announced itself for this project and the operating system describes it as this project's engine run, --path on the project and no editor flag, started before it announced; otherwise nothing is signalled and the answer says which of those failed. The run this server holds is ended the ordinary way whether or not its number is given. Only for op stop.

profile.description: start: profile the run's GDScript with the engine's own script profiler from its start, for editor_run profile to answer which functions took the time. A run this server starts dials the process that keeps it as its debugger, on loopback, with breakpoints and error breaks skipped so it never stops to wait; a game the editor plays is profiled through the editor's debugger session. Needs an engine built with debugging, which the editor binary is and a release export template is not. The start answers profile.on and, under profile.totals, how the numbers will arrive. Default false. Only for op start.

projectPath.description: Absolute path to the project directory, the one holding project.godot. stop, wait, profile: optional, the project whose run is meant; a run of another project is refused rather than touched.

runtimeWaitMs.description: start: how long to wait for the game to announce its runtime before answering. Default 5000, or half as long again as the slowest of the last five boots of the same scene when that is more, up to 60000: the server notes how long each game took to announce, per scene and for the main scene when none is named, since a boot moves with the load on the machine, so a scene that boots slowly is waited for from its second start on without being asked to, and a harness scene that announces late sets nothing for the main scene. What it waits for is the first frame, so everything the game does before drawing one is inside it, including work the args just asked for: a flag that simulates six years of game time before anything is drawn makes the announcement that late, on a project that announces promptly without it. Raise it for such a run rather than reading runtime listening false as a fault. 0 does not wait at all, which is the one to pass for a scene that announces nothing by construction, such as a bench that prints and quits. Only for op start.

savesIn.description: An absolute directory for this run's user://, so a game that saves writes nowhere near the copy somebody plays: opening a save writes the one being left, and a game that autosaves writes on its own. Godot takes no flag for it, so this is the environment, and the run is started by this server rather than played by the editor, which cannot be given one. It does not have to exist: the engine makes it, and the Godot/app_userdata/<project> tree under it, measured on 4.7.2. Whatever the run, runtime.userDir in the answer is the directory user:// is, as the game's engine resolved it. On macOS the engine reads user:// off HOME and ignores it, also measured, and the answer says so under savesNote rather than leaving the caller to find out from the player's save list. Only for ops start, check.

scene.description: A scene to run instead of the main scene. Only for ops start, check.

silent.description: start: run the game with no sound out of the machine, by starting the engine with --audio-driver Dummy: every stream still plays and every playback position still advances, so what is playing can still be asked. The editor takes no engine flags for a game it plays, so a silent windowed run is started by this server, whose keeper is its debugger rather than the editor. A headless run, check's included, is silent already, and so is a test run. Default true, for an exported build too: pass false to hear the game, which a windowed run with the editor connected then plays through the editor. Only for op start.

since.description: profile: "mark" answers only what was added after the mark that mark: true set in this run: per function the calls and self and total milliseconds since it, with the functions that added no call left out, frames and coveredMs since it, and callersOf read off the same difference. Refused when no mark was set in this run, or when the profile holds less than it did at the mark, which is a profiler started again since. Only for op profile.

suites.description: start: gdUnit4 suites to play instead of a scene, a suite file or a test directory inside the project or a list of them, as project_test's path takes them. They run in the tests addon's suites scene through the runner gdharness test uses, so with profile: true the profile names what the suites cost by function, which project_test and gdharness test cannot show, since the profiler never sees a script run. The run quits with gdUnit4's exit code; read it with editor_output until running is false, then profile. Takes no scene or executable, and needs gdUnit4 and the tests addon of this release in the project. Only for op start.

timeoutMs.description: check: how long to give the boot before it is called hung. Default 60000. wait: how long to wait for the run to end before answering anyway. Default 600000. Only for ops check, wait.

visible.description: start: on Windows, show the window on the desktop in use. By default a windowed run this server starts goes on a desktop of its own, where it renders and runtime_capture works but the window never shows and never takes the keyboard. A game a visible editor plays opens on the desktop in use, and one a hidden editor (editor_launch hidden: true) plays goes on its desktop. Elsewhere than Windows the window shows either way. Default false. Only for op start.

name: editor_run
title: Run the game
